# Apps

Browser tools that run entirely on your own machine. Nothing is uploaded,
nothing is installed, and none of them need a radio attached.

## [Signal Explorer](apps/signal-explorer/index.qmd)

A radio simulator you can watch and hear. Pick a mode and it builds the signal
from the theory up, showing the audio going in, I and Q against time, the
constellation, the spectrum and a waterfall, all drawn from the same samples so
every view is the same instant.

Sliders for tuning error, noise, gain and fading. Turn the sound on and you can
hear both the audio going in and what comes back out of the receiver, which
makes the effect of noise, mistuning and overmodulation audible rather than
only visible.

It covers the analogue modes (AM, FM, SSB in both sidebands, double sideband
suppressed carrier) and the digital ones (CW, RTTY, FT8, BPSK through 8PSK,
16-QAM and 64-QAM). Every panel of Figures 4, 5 and 6 in
*Seeing signals: I and Q from first principles*, in the September 2026 issue of
RadCom, is there under its own number, and each has its own link.

Each mode shows where its numbers came from: the sample rate, tuning and
filtering of the flowgraph that made the matching capture, or, where a value is
a published standard rather than a measured one, it says so.

## [Bench Test](https://bench.g0lft.org)

Interactive pages for the technical part of the amateur radio syllabus, at
[bench.g0lft.org](https://bench.g0lft.org). Each page turns the circuits from a
syllabus group into working instruments.

There are controls for the component values. Move one and the page solves the
circuit again from a nodal analysis: the readings update, the waveforms redraw,
the working underneath substitutes the new values, and the charge moving round
the schematic changes speed to match the current in each branch.

The pages work offline once loaded, and are meant to sit alongside a course and
the books rather than replace them. Tuned circuits and semiconductors are up so
far, with further syllabus groups to come.
